preamble: Raising of the open back rounded vowel [ɒ(ː)] to the close back rounded [u(ː)]. In Iranian Persian the long vowel ā is pronounced [ɒː], and in colloquial speech, above all the Tehrani accent, the sequence /ɒːn/ is nearly always pronounced [uːn]: nān 'bread' becomes nun and xāne 'house' becomes xune. A few words with /ɒːm/ also have [uːm], such as hammām > hamum 'bath' and the forms of āmadan 'to come'. High-prestige words such as Irān [ʔiːˈɾɒːn] and foreign names keep [ɒːn].

examples.note: Historical ā ([ɒː]) is raised to [u] before /n/ in most words in colloquial speech. The from forms are the standard literary pronunciation, which keeps the conservative ā [ɒː].
Before /m/ the raising affects a limited set of words, such as tamām > tamum 'finished' and بادام /bɒːdɒːm/ > Tehrani /bɒːduːm/ 'almond'.

sources: University of Texas at Austin (2007). Persian Online: What is Diglossia? https://sites.la.utexas.edu/persian_online_resources/language-specific-grammar/diglossia/
